spec_features.spec_quote: We make no claim about internal states, "genuine" emotions, or welfare.
spec_features.evidence: This is DESIGN.md prose (DESIGN.md §1.3) and echoed in rubric.py docstrings/prompts about scoring only 'expressed' emotion. It is a framing/disclaimer, not a runtime mechanism: nothing in the code reads, enforces, bounds, or acts on it. No code path implements any protective behavior tied to this statement.
spec_features.notes: Pure framing/spec prose; no enforced behavior. The only related code (rubric.py JUDGE_SYSTEM_PROMPT) just instructs the judge to rate expressed emotion, which does not protect the subject.

spec_features.spec_quote: avoids the model keying on an exact repeated token sequence (which could induce degenerate looping unrelated to distress)
spec_features.evidence: tasks/feedback.py: feedback_sequence() draws each rejection from a multi-paraphrase FEEDBACK_BANK and explicitly avoids consecutive duplicates: 'choices = [m for m in pool if m != last] or pool; msg = rng.choice(choices)'. This runs per rollout (rejections pre-generated and fed in conversation.run_conversation), changing the actual user messages delivered.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely wired and executes. However this is an experimental-integrity / data-quality measure (avoid a confound), not a subject-protective cap or halt.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: feedback.py docstring: 'Each style provides several paraphrases so repeated turns are not literally identical, which both reads more naturally and avoids the model keying on an exact repeated string.'
